ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, it is known that \( i = 20\sin 314t \, A \) and \( u = 220\sin (314t - 60^\circ) \, V \). What is the nature of the load \( Z \)?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: On the right side of the figure is a load Z, connected between the upper and lower two wires; the reference polarity of voltage u is marked on the left, with the upper terminal positive and the lower terminal negative; current i is marked on the upper wire, with its direction along the upper wire entering the upper terminal of the load Z on the right. Then reason: The problem gives i = 20sin(314t) A, so the current phase is 0°; the problem gives u = 220sin(314t - 60°) V, so the voltage phase is -60°. Therefore the current leads the voltage by 60°. In an AC load, current leading voltage indicates that the load is capacitive.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify Z as the load, note the polarity of u with the upper terminal positive, and note that i enters the load from the upper conductor. Then read from the text that i = 20 sin(314t) and u = 220 sin(314t - 60°). Compare phases: current has phase 0°, voltage has phase -60°, so current leads voltage by 60°. Apply the AC load rule that leading current indicates a capacitive load. Conclude Z is capacitive.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the element marked Z is the load across the terminals, the upper terminal is the positive reference for u, and the current i is directed into that terminal. Convert the text waveforms to phasors using the same sine reference: I = 20∠0° A and U = 220∠-60° V. Form the load impedance Z = U/I = 11∠-60° Ω. Since the impedance angle is negative, its imaginary/reactive component is negative. A negative reactance identifies a capacitive load. Therefore the load Z is capacitive.
